column1: l4/dusche|shower|The shower is small.|
l4/badewanne|bathtub|The bathtub is big.|baden = to take a bath + Wanne = tub.
l4/waschbecken|washbasin, sink|The washbasin is small.|Ending -en: the plural doesn't change.
l4/farbe|colour|What colour is the table?|
l4/schwarz|black|The chairs are black.|schw- sounds like "shv"; a final z = "ts".
l4/weiss|white|Milk is white.|ei sounds like "eye". ⚠ Spelt the same as ich weiß (I know).
l4/grau|grey|The lamp is grey.|
l4/rot|red|The sofa is red.|
l4/blau|blue|The carpet is blue.|au sounds like "ow".
l4/gruen|green|The armchair is green.|Long ü.
l4/gelb|yellow|The banana is yellow.|A final b sounds like p: "gelp".
l4/braun|brown|The wardrobe is brown.|au sounds like "ow".
l4/hell-dunkel|light- / dark- (before a colour)|The sofa is dark blue.|Written as one word with the colour: hellrot = light red, dunkelblau = dark blue.

l4/gefallen|to please, to like|How do you like the sofa?|The thing you like is the subject: Der Tisch gefällt mir. Die Stühle gefallen mir. (dir = you informal, Ihnen = you polite; just learn the phrase.)
l4/finden|to find, to think (opinion)|I think the sofa is very good.|Used to give an opinion. Das finde ich auch. = I think so too.
l4/wie-gefaellt|How do you like …? (dir = informal, Ihnen = polite)||
l4/das-finde-ich-auch|I think so too.||
l4/schau-mal|Look! (Schau mal = informal, Schauen Sie mal = polite)||
l4/bewertung|very good – good – quite good – OK – not so good||
l4/tausend|1,000 · one thousand||au sounds like "ow". Written as one word: zweitausend (2,000). German uses a full stop to group thousands (1.000).
l4/million|1,000,000 · one million|A million euros!|eine Million (separate, because it's a noun); zwei Millionen.
l4/zentimeter|centimetre (cm)|The bed is 140 centimetres wide.|z = ts. Short form cm.
l4/meter|metre (m)|The table is two metres long.|Long e; a final -er sounds soft like "a".
l4/quadratmeter|square metre (m², qm)|The flat is 60 square metres.|qu = "kv". Short form m² or qm.
l4/mal|times (×); time (occasion)|The bed is 90 by 200 centimetres.|60 × 120 cm is said sechzig mal hundertzwanzig Zentimeter.
l4/lang|long|The hall is three metres long.|Question: Wie lang ist …? Opposite: kurz (short).
l4/hoch|high, tall|The shelf is 180 centimetres high.|Long o; ch after o is throaty. Question: Wie hoch ist …?
l4/ungefaehr|about, approximately|The bathroom is about six square metres.|Same as circa (ca.). Opposite: genau (exactly, Lesson 2).
l4/handy|mobile phone|My mobile number is new.|"Handy" means mobile phone only in German; say "hen-dee".
l4/arbeit|work; workplace|I'm at work.|Usually singular. bei der Arbeit = at work.
l4/zu-hause|at home|I'm at home.|
l4/meine-nummer|My home number is … · My mobile number is …||
l4/anzeige|advert, classified ad|The ad is from a private owner.|Wohnungsanzeige = flat-for-rent/sale ad in a newspaper or online.
l4/ehepaar|married couple|A nice married couple is looking for a flat.|Ehe = marriage + Paar = couple. (Ehemann, Ehefrau: Lesson 2.)
l4/nett|nice, kind|The family is very nice.|tt signals a short e.
l4/suchen|to look for, to search|We're looking for a flat.|Long u; ch after u is throaty.
l4/vermieten|to rent out, to let|I'm renting out a room.|ver- sounds like "fer" (v = f) and isn't stressed. Related: die Miete = rent; mieten = to rent.
l4/apartment|small flat, studio|The studio is small but nice.|
l4/garten|garden|The garden is very beautiful.|Plural Gärten.
l4/garage|garage|The garage is new.|A final -ge sounds like "zheh", as in French.
l4/stock|floor, storey|The flat is on the 3rd floor.|Singular for floors: im 3. Stock = on the 3rd floor. The ground floor is das Erdgeschoss.
l4/raum|room; space|The room is bright.|Raum is more formal than Zimmer and common in ads: Wohnraum = living space.
l4/circa|about, approximately (ca.)|The flat is about 60 square metres.|Short form ca.; say "tseer-ka". Same as ungefähr.
l4/privat|private|The flat is offered privately.|von privat = from a private owner (not an agency). v is said as v (loanword).
l4/ab|from (a time) on|The room costs from 300 euros.|ab sofort = from now on; ab 19 Uhr = from 7 p.m.
l4/sofort|immediately, right away|I need a flat right away.|
l4/maximal|at most, maximum (max.)|The room costs 400 euros at most.|Short form max. Opposite: minimal.
l4/anruf|phone call|There's a call for you.|Ads often end with: Ich freue mich auf Ihren Anruf. (= I look forward to your call.)
l4/moebliert|furnished|The room is furnished.|It already has Möbel. Opposite: unmöbliert. Short form möbl.
l4/tv|TV|The studio is furnished, with TV.|Say "tay-fow" (T-V). In ads: mit TV = with a TV. Same as der Fernseher.
l4/miete|rent|The rent is 650 euros.|ie = long ee (different from Mitte = middle).
l4/bezahlen|to pay|I pay the rent.|be- is not stressed.
l4/kaution|deposit||Usually 2–3 months' rent (Monatsmieten).
l4/nebenkosten|extra costs, utilities||Short form NK. Plural only.
l4/warmmiete|rent including heating and utilities||Opposite: die Kaltmiete (rent without extras).
l4/einbaukueche|fitted kitchen||Short form EBK.
l4/buch|book|The book is new.|Long u; ch after u is throaty. Plural Bücher.
l4/heft|exercise book, notebook|I need an exercise book.|
l4/stift|pen, pencil|Here's a pen.|st at the start sounds like "sht".
l4/computer|computer|The computer is new.|The plural doesn't change.
l4/tablet|tablet|The tablet is small.|
l4/tagebuch|diary|The diary is old.|Tag (day) + Buch (book).
l4/schreibtisch|desk|My desk is big.|schreiben = to write + Tisch = table. schr- sounds like "shr".
l4/schreibtischlampe|desk lamp|The desk lamp is red.|
l4/schreibtischstuhl|desk chair|The desk chair is blue.|
l4/holz|wood|The table is made of wood.|aus Holz = made of wood.
l4/viel|much / many|I have many exercise books.|viel + uncountable (viel Platz); viele + plural (viele Hefte).
l4/voll|full; crowded|The desk is full.|Opposite: leer (empty).
l4/platz|space, room; square|I need a lot of space.|Usually singular: viel Platz = lots of room. (Platz is also "square", plural Plätze.)
l4/ziemlich|quite, fairly|My room is quite small.|ie = long ee; a final -lich sounds like "-likh".
l4/egal|doesn't matter, all the same|It doesn't matter.|
l4/lieben|to love|I love my flat.|ie = long ee. Stronger than "gern haben".
l4/immer|always|My desk is always full.|mm signals a short i.
l4/hausaufgabe|homework|I'm doing my homework.|Often plural: Hausaufgaben machen = to do homework.
l4/glauben|to believe, to think|I think he's already very old.|
l4/besonders|especially, particularly|The lamp is especially nice.|
l4/welch|which|What colour is your desk?|welcher + der word · welches + das word · welche + die word and plural.
l4/ein-paar|a few, a couple of|A few books, a few pens.|
l4/wirklich|really|The room is really nice.|
l4/wichtig|important|The desk is very important.|
l4/ordnung|tidiness, order|My place is tidy.|Bei mir ist Ordnung. = My place is neat and tidy.
l4/leer|empty|The desk is empty.|
l5/machen|to do, to make|Lara is giving a presentation.|ch after a is throaty: "ma-khen". Was machst du? = What are you doing?
l5/praesentation|presentation|Lara is giving a presentation.|Stress the last syllable. eine Präsentation machen = to give a presentation.
l5/fruehstuecken|to have breakfast|We have breakfast together.|früh (early) + stücken. das Frühstück = breakfast.
l5/einkaufen|to go shopping|I go shopping at the supermarket.|Separable verb: kaufen … ein. The prefix ein- is stressed.
l5/spazieren-gehen|to go for a walk|Lara goes for a walk.|spazieren goes to the end like a prefix: Lara geht spazieren.
l5/aufraeumen|to tidy up|She tidies up the kitchen.|Separable verb: räumen … auf. äu sounds like "oy": "roy-men".
l5/aufstehen|to get up, to stand up|Lara gets up early.|Separable verb: stehen … auf. st after the prefix is still "sht": "OWF-shtay-en".
l5/gehen|to go, to walk|Lara goes to her German course.|zum = zu dem, zur = zu der, ins = in das: set phrases zum Deutschkurs, zur Arbeit, ins Bett.
l5/oder|or|She goes for a walk or goes shopping.|
l5/arbeiten|to work|Sofia works a lot.|Add -e- before -st / -t to make it easier to say: du arbeitest, er arbeitet. Related: die Arbeit (Lesson 4).
l5/muede|tired, sleepy|In the evening Sofia is tired.|Long ü. müde = tired because you need sleep.
l5/anrufen|to call (on the phone)|Lara calls her family.|Separable verb: rufen … an. No preposition needed: Lara ruft ihre Familie an (ihre = her).
l5/frueh|early|I get up early.|Opposite: spät (late).
l5/supermarkt|supermarket|She shops at the supermarket.|
l5/fernsehen|to watch TV|She watches a bit of TV.|Separable, and e changes to ie with du and er/sie (sehen: siehst, sieht), like sprechen → sprichst in Lesson 1.
l5/mit|with|Sofia has breakfast with Lara and Lili.|mit + person: mit Lara, mit Lili.
l5/spielen|to play|She plays with Lili.|sp- at the start sounds like "shp": "SHPEE-len".
l5/hoeren|to hear, to listen to|Lara listens to music.|ö: lips rounded as for "o", tongue as for "ay".
l5/musik|music|I like listening to music.|Stress the last syllable. Usually no plural.
l5/abendessen|dinner, supper|Lara cooks dinner.|Abend (evening) + essen. Related: das Frühstück, das Mittagessen.
l5/deutschkurs|German course|Lara goes to her German course.|
l5/ins-bett-gehen|to go to bed|Sofia goes to bed.|ins = in das (set phrase). Same pattern: ins Kino gehen (go to the cinema).
l5/zur-arbeit-gehen|to go to work|Sofia goes to work.|zur = zu der.
l5/was-machst-du-gern|What do you like doing? (du = informal, Sie = polite)||
l5/uhr|clock, watch; o'clock|That's a clock.|Say "oo-a" (soft final r). Uhr is a clock and also "o'clock": sieben Uhr.
l5/spaet|late|It's already late.|Long ä: "shpayt". Asking the time: Wie spät ist es? (literally "how late is it?"). Opposite: früh.
l5/erst|only (not until)|No, it's only quarter to twelve.|erst = only…, less than expected. The opposite of schon.
l5/viertel|quarter; 15 minutes|It's quarter past three.|Viertel nach drei = 3:15; Viertel vor vier = 3:45. ie = long ee.
l5/vor|to (… minutes to the hour)|It's ten to eight.|fünf vor zwei = 1:55. Just like English "five to two".
l5/nach|past (… minutes past the hour)|It's five past three.|zehn nach zwei = 2:10. Just like English "ten past two".
l5/halb|half|It's half past eight.|⚠ halb zwei = 1:30 (half way to two), NOT 2:30. Always name the NEXT hour. A final b sounds like p.
l5/zeichnen|to draw|Draw the time.|ei = "eye"; add -e- as with arbeiten: du zeichnest.
l5/kurz|short; just (before / after)|It's just before twelve.|kurz vor zwölf = just before 12 (11:58); kurz nach zwölf = just after 12 (12:03).
l5/gleich|right away; almost (the hour)|It's almost twelve.|gleich zwölf = nearly 12 o'clock. Also "in a moment": Ich komme gleich.
l5/wie-spaet|What time is it?||
l5/es-ist-halb|It's half past seven.||Remember: halb acht = 7:30.
l5/ist-es-schon|Is it twelve already? – No, it's only eleven.||
l5/montag|Monday|I work on Monday.|All seven days are der. A final tag sounds like "tahk".
l5/dienstag|Tuesday|On Tuesday Tim plays football.|ie = long ee.
l5/mittwoch|Wednesday|On Wednesday I study German.|Mitte (middle) + Woche (week) = midweek. A final ch is throaty.
l5/donnerstag|Thursday|On Thursday I call Mum.|
l5/freitag|Friday|On Friday I go shopping.|
l5/samstag|Saturday|On Saturday I cook.|In northern and eastern Germany people also say der Sonnabend.
l5/sonntag|Sunday|On Sunday I sleep in.|
l5/woche|week|A week has seven days.|ch after o is throaty.
l5/wochenende|weekend|At the weekend I sleep in.|= Saturday + Sunday. am Wochenende = at the weekend.
l5/termin|appointment|The appointment is on Friday.|Stress the last syllable. Termin = a doctor's appointment, a meeting… (not a date).
l5/terminkalender|diary, planner|My diary is full.|
l5/naechst|next (nächste Woche = next week)|Next week I have no time.|The ending -e because Woche is a die word (adjective endings come later).
l5/wann|when|When does the course start?|Asks for a time. ⚠ wann ≠ wenn.
l5/am|on (a day), in (part of the day)|On Monday I study German.|am = an dem. Used with days and parts of the day: am Montag, am Abend (exception: in der Nacht).
l5/um|at (a clock time)|I get up at seven o'clock.|um + time: um halb neun, um zwei Uhr.
l5/von-bis|from … to/until …|The course is from Monday to Friday.|A time span: von Montag bis Freitag, von acht bis drei Uhr.
l5/party|party|I'm having a party on Friday.|
l5/zeit|time; free time|Are you free on Saturday?|Hast du Zeit? = Are you free? Ich habe keine Zeit. = I don't have time.
l5/fussball|football, soccer|Tim plays football on Tuesday.|ß = s, long u. Fußball spielen = to play football.
l5/anfangen|to begin, to start|The German course starts at nine.|Separable verb: fangen … an. a → ä with du and er/sie (fängst, fängt).
l5/passen|to suit, to fit|The appointment suits me well.|Das passt gut. = That works / That suits me.
l5/schlafen|to sleep|On Sunday he sleeps in.|a → ä with du and er/sie. lange schlafen = to sleep in.
l5/intensivkurs|intensive course|The intensive course is from Monday to Friday.|
l5/mama|mum, mom|Tim calls Mum.|
l5/papa|dad|Dad works on Saturday.|
l5/hast-du-zeit|Are you free? / Do you have time?||Inviting or arranging: Hast du am Freitag Zeit?
l5/das-passt-gut|That suits me. / That works.||
l5/da-habe-ich-keine-zeit|I'm not free then.||A polite way to turn down a time.
l5/um-wie-viel-uhr|At what time …?||Asks for an exact time. Answer: Um halb elf. / Um elf Uhr.
l5/morgen|morning|In the morning I get up early.|Same word as in Guten Morgen! am Morgen = in the morning.
l5/vormittag|late morning (about 9–12)|In the morning I study German.|
l5/mittag|midday, noon (about 12–2 p.m.)|At midday I eat with Anna.|
l5/nachmittag|afternoon|In the afternoon I go for a walk.|Different from Mittag (midday).
l5/abend|evening|In the evening I watch TV.|You already know Guten Abend; am Abend = in the evening.
l5/nacht|night|At night I sleep.|⚠ Exception: in der Nacht (not am Nacht). Plural Nächte.
l5/kino|cinema|In the evening I go to the cinema.|ins Kino gehen = to go to the cinema.
l5/chatten|to chat (online)|At night Max chats.|ch is said "tsh" as in English. Add -e- as with arbeiten: er chattet.
l5/raten|to guess|The others guess: what's wrong?|a → ä with du and er/sie: du rätst, er rät.
l5/jeder|every, each|I get up at six every morning.|With time: jeden Tag / Morgen / Abend (der words), jede Nacht / Woche (die words).
l5/sport|sport|In the afternoon he does sport.|Sport machen = to do sport.
l5/computerspiel|computer game|In the afternoon he plays computer games.|
l5/doch|yes (contradicting a negative)|You don't have time? – Yes, I do!|Doch = "on the contrary, yes": Du stehst nicht um sechs auf. – Doch! (Yes, I do!)
l5/in-der-nacht|at night||Special preposition: in der (not am).
l5/jeden-tag|every day|I study German every day.|
l5/ich-glaube|I think …||Used to guess: Ich glaube, du stehst nicht jeden Tag um sechs auf. Answer: Stimmt. / Doch.
l5/ausgehen|to go out||
l5/losgehen|to set off, to start||
l5/treffen|to meet||e → i: triffst, trifft.
l5/lesen|to read||e → ie: liest.
l5/telefonieren|to talk on the phone||
l5/joggen|to jog||Said with "j" as in English.
l5/manchmal|sometimes||
l5/mittagessen|lunch||
l5/mittagspause|lunch break||
l5/cafe|café|The café is open every day.|Stress the last syllable; a final é sounds like "ay".
l5/taeglich|daily, every day|The library is open every day.|= jeden Tag. -lich sounds like "-likh".
l5/fahrrad|bicycle|The bike is new.|fahren (to ride) + Rad (wheel). Plural Fahrräder.
l5/bibliothek|library|The library is open on Monday.|Stress the last syllable.
l5/feiertag|public holiday|On public holidays the library is closed.|Feier (celebration) + Tag. An Feiertagen = on public holidays.
l5/geschlossen|closed|The café is closed on Sunday.|Opposite: geöffnet.
l5/ansage|announcement (over a speaker, on the phone)|Listen to the announcement.|
l5/offiziell|official|Official: nineteen thirty.|offizielle Uhrzeit = official time (24-hour clock).
l5/wann-ist-geoeffnet|When is … open?||
l5/film|film, movie|The film starts at eight.|Short i, one syllable: "film".
l5/sehen|to see, to watch|I can see the ship.|e → ie with du and er/sie. Related to fernsehen.
l5/museum|museum|The museum is closed on Monday.|Plural: die Museen.
l5/geoeffnet|open|The café is open every day.|Opposite: geschlossen.
l5/schiff|ship, boat|The ship leaves in the afternoon.|
l5/tour|tour|The tour starts at three o'clock.|Said "toor".
l5/kaufhaus|department store|The department store is open Monday to Saturday.|
l5/europa|Europe|Germany is in Europe.|eu = "oy": "oy-ROH-pa".
l5/kennenlernen|to get to know|I'm getting to know the city.|kennen (to know) + lernen. Separable: Ich lerne Hamburg kennen. The prefix kennen- is stressed.
l5/abfahrt|departure|Departure is at ten thirty.|On timetables for trains and boats: Abfahrt = departure.
l5/erwachsene|adult|For adults the tour costs eight euros.|On price lists: Erwachsene (adults) / Kinder (children).
l5/plan|plan|My plan for Saturday is good.|einen Plan machen = to make a plan.
l6/ausflug|trip, day trip, outing|On Sunday we're going on a trip.|einen Ausflug machen = to go on a trip. au sounds like "ow"; the plural has ü: die Ausflüge.
l6/auto|car|I like driving.|au sounds like "ow". Auto fahren = to drive / go by car.
l6/fahren|to go (by vehicle), to drive, to ride|My father drives every day.|a → ä with du and er/sie: fährst, fährt. Auto fahren, Ski fahren, Fahrrad fahren.
l6/wandern|to hike|We go hiking at the weekend.|w sounds like v: "VAN-dern". Long walks in nature.
l6/picknick|picnic|On Saturday we're having a picnic.|ein Picknick machen = to have a picnic. ck sounds like k.
l6/gitarre|guitar|My brother plays the guitar.|Stress the middle. Gitarre spielen = to play the guitar (no article).
l6/fotografieren|to take photos|Mia likes taking photos.|Verbs in -ieren are always stressed on "ie" (like telefonieren in Lesson 5). Related: das Foto.
l6/sonne|sun; sunshine|The sun is shining today.|Usually no plural. Die Sonne scheint. = It's sunny.
l6/scheinen|to shine|The sun shines in the morning.|sch sounds like "sh", ei like "eye". Usually about die Sonne.
l6/regnen|to rain|It's raining today.|Only with es: Es regnet. Long e; say both g and n: "RAYG-nen". Noun: der Regen.
l6/schneien|to snow|It's snowing a lot today.|Only with es: Es schneit. Noun: der Schnee.
l6/wolke|cloud|There are no clouds today.|w sounds like v.
l6/wetter|weather|The weather is nice today.|Singular only. A final -er is soft like "a": "VET-ta". Wie ist das Wetter? = What's the weather like?
l6/heute|today|Today I'm tired.|eu sounds like "oy": "HOY-teh".
l6/viele|many (before plural nouns)|He has many books.|v sounds like f: "FEE-leh". viele + plural: viele Wolken, viele Bücher. With uncountables use viel: viel Wind, viel Zeit.
l6/vergessen|to forget|Lili forgets the guitar.|ver- sounds like "fer" and isn't stressed. e → i with du and er/sie (like sprechen → du sprichst).
l6/bringen|to bring|I'll bring the bread.|ng as in "sing", no separate g sound.
l6/nachricht|message; (plural) the news|Mia writes a message.|eine Nachricht schreiben = to write a message. ch after a is throaty, ch after i is soft.
l6/grad|degree (temperature)|It's 20 degrees today.|No change after a number: 25 Grad. For temperatures: Es sind 25 Grad (use sind).
l6/warm|warm|It's warm today.|Es ist warm. Hotter is heiß.
l6/kalt|cold|It's cold in the evening.|Opposite: warm / heiß.
l6/windig|windy|It's windy today.|w sounds like v; a final -ig sounds like "-ikh": "VIN-dikh". Noun: der Wind.
l6/bewoelkt|cloudy|It's cloudy in the morning.|From die Wolke. Es ist bewölkt. = Es gibt viele Wolken.
l6/wie-ist-das-wetter|What's the weather like?|What's the weather like in Berlin? – Good. The sun is shining.|Answers: Gut. / Schön. / Nicht so gut. / Schlecht.
l6/es-gibt|there is / there are|There's a supermarket here.|Es gibt + noun: Es gibt viele Wolken. Es gibt einen Park. gibt is the er/sie/es form of geben (e → i).
l6/einen-ausflug-machen|to go on a trip|Shall we go on a trip on Saturday?|einen because der Ausflug is the object of machen (accusative).
